text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Editorial: Contrary to speculations of some foreign media on President Franjo Tudjman's poor health, he is feeling very well and is performing his duties normally.
- U.N. investigators have identified 60 of 200 bodies exhumed from the Ovcara mass grave in Eastern Slavonia and confirmed that most were Vukovar hospital patients.
- Introducing the kuna into the last Serb-held enclave of Eastern Slavonia is one of the National Bank of Croatia's priorities this year.
- Union of textile and leather industry employers to close business for 10 minutes today to warn the government of the collapse looming on the horizon.
- Independent Radio 101 is sure to be awarded one of two frequencies for capital Zagreb in a new tender, sources reveal.
- Tobacco industry and cigarette consumption are on the decline. In 1996, Croatia produced 11,500 tonnes of cigarettes, compared to 12,154 tonnes in 1995.
- The central bank is satisfied with last year's low inflation but is worried about a huge 1997 state budget and planned foreign borrowing.

- National Judicial Council rejected the request of the suspended Supreme Court head Krunoslav Olujic, allegedly involved in sex with minors, that disiciplinary proceedings against him be open to public.

- Croatia has no interest to favour Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic but Serbian opposition offers no guarantees for the preservation of peace at the moment, says Tudjman's social affairs adviser Zlatko Canjuga.
- Germany's KfW bank to grant a 13 million German marks five-year loan for computerisation of Zagreb airport. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4551840
